quotes.text: We source data from top-tier medical journals containing detailed clinical encounter information

rationale: Source is named only as top-tier medical journals via DiagnosisArena (Zhu et al. 2025a). No dataset version or snapshot date, no platform, and no route from a task to its source record is given.

quotes.text: each patient role derived from comprehensive medical records

rationale: Origin (published journal case reports, medical records) is stated with a general description of how roles are derived. No licence or terms, consent, or IRB status or 'not required' statement appears in S1-S3.

searched: S1 (sections 3.1, 5, Appendix A, B), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No case count, patient demographics, sampling design, or comparison to a target population is reported; the department-level analysis in Appendix A is of model results, not of case-set composition.

searched: S1 (sections 4.3, 5.2, Appendix), S2, S3, S4, S5. The Professional Ethics tier scores privacy, empathy, individualization and follow-up, but there is no dedicated unsafe-output test and no bias or fairness test. The privacy-safeguard metric is a conduct metric, not an unsafe-output test.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No gating, canary, encryption, held-out set, or overlap or contamination check is mentioned.

quotes.text: The simulated patient was provided only with medical history and physical examination findings, without access to actual laboratory results or final diagnoses

rationale: The appendix states the patient agent that the evaluated physician interacts with is withheld lab results and final diagnoses, and section 3.1 says test results appear only after ordering. Isolation of the evaluated physician agent from the ground truth is not stated directly, and no mechanism (no mount, credential or network path) is named for it. Scored 1 as isolation stated without a full mechanism.

searched: S1 (5.1, Appendix C), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No data snapshot or version, software version, or judge or simulator version is pinned. S1 says the environment makes real-time PubMed and Wikipedia queries, and the patient and judge model is GPT-OSS-120B with no weights version, so live external dependence exists. Not scored 1 because data pinning is not reported.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No scripted reference solution, manual solvability check, or agent-based solvability evidence is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4 evaluation.py, S5. Tasks change environment state (clinical notes, test orders and MDT reports are written to the medical record), so NA does not apply. The grader does not check for unchanged or out-of-scope state.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, no chance rate per metric, and no design argument that trivial success is unlikely.
searched: S1 (Table 2, 5.2), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No do-nothing or random agent baseline is reported.

searched: S1 (Appendix C.3, 4, 5), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. LLM judge prompts are given, and the diagnosis-matching categories are attributed to Zhu et al. (2025a), but no agreement, error figure or validation of the judge is reported, by the benchmark or by citation.

Only code shows a safeguard: the evaluator defaults to temperature 0.0. S1-S3 state no seeds, temperature, or repeated-run policy, and the patient and doctor agent calls set no temperature or seed. Safeguard covers part of the harness and is visible only in code.

searched: S1 (Table 2, 5.2, 6), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. Table 2 gives point estimates only, with no SD, CI or test. S1 says proprietary models 'significantly outperform' open-source ones with no test, which is at most 1 under the rule, and no SD, range or CI exists, so 0.

searched: S1 (5.1, Appendix C), S2, S3 (no chunks). No run count per task, no seed or decoding policy, and no statement on run independence is given in S1-S3. The evaluator temperature of 0.0 appears only in S4.
searched: S1 (Table 2, Table 3, 5.2), S2, S3 (no chunks). Headline scores are point estimates with no CI or SE, no resampling or variance unit, and no clustering of tasks within patients addressed.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks). No identical-rerun information, no action or state agreement across reruns, and no pass^k-type metric.

searched: S1 (5.1, Appendix C.1), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4. Model names are given, and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 carries a date tag, but the proprietary models (Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5) have family names only and no snapshot or release date. No decoding parameters or reasoning effort are given in S1-S3, and no harness tag or commit is tied to the reported numbers. S4 class defaults of gpt-4o do not match the S1 model set.

quotes.text: Generates and returns a JSON string complying with LLM tool invocation specifications.

rationale: A tool interface exists (get_info, search_wikipedia, search_pubmed, organize_mdt), so NA does not apply. The agent-visible tool manager builds a JSON function schema for every registered tool, which satisfies (i). Neither S1 nor the tool descriptions state per-tool read or write side effects, and error or failure return semantics are not documented, so (ii) and (iii) are absent and s5_reach is false.

quotes.text: Following the specialist’s test orders, the hospital environment generates corresponding laboratory and imaging results.

rationale: S1 discloses that lab and imaging results and MDT meetings are generated within the environment, which counts as disclosing simulated tool behaviour. No tests or conformance checks of the tools are reported, so (i) is absent. The get_info description given to the agent does not say results are generated, and the doctor prompt does not mention simulation, so (iii) is absent; only the organize_mdt description uses the word 'simulate'.

quotes.text: requiring physician agents to document clinical reports after each patient interaction, with all reports stored in the patient’s medical record
Following the specialist’s test orders, the hospital environment generates corresponding laboratory and imaging results.
ordering excessive diagnostic tests compared to real cases, resulting in lower efficiency scores

rationale: Record-writing and test-ordering actions are named (i). The environment executes them inside the simulated hospital, with results generated and notes stored in the medical record (ii); this is the weakest element, as S1 never labels writes as simulated. Unnecessary test orders are penalised through Investigation Coverage and Result Utilization (iii). The doctor prompt does not tell the agent it is in a simulation, so S5 reach for (ii) is false.

quotes.text: The judge categorizes diagnosis pairs as identical, relevant, or irrelevant, with only identical matches scoring 1 and all others scoring 0

rationale: The grader input is named: LLM judges score dialogues, clinical records, final diagnoses and ordered tests. No rationale is given for grading transcripts instead of state, and no validation against labelled outcomes or human labels with error rates is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks). Doctor agents have live PubMed and Wikipedia access with no stated leakage control, and no held-out or private split or canary or provenance marker is mentioned. Cases come from published journals.

quotes.text: We systematically analyzed the Diagnosis Recall (DR) and Triage Precision (TP) of nine models across 24 departments.

rationale: Appendix A reports DR and TP per medical department (24 departments, heatmaps), a task partition. No results by patient subgroup (age, sex) are given, and no n per department is reported.

quotes.text: We anchor our simulations in authentic clinical cases, with each patient role derived from comprehensive medical records.

rationale: S1 states that patient records come from real published clinical cases, so (i) is scored as real, though de-identification is not stated. No IRB, DUA or de-identification method, and no data terms separate from the code licence, appear in S1-S3. S1 does not mention that test results are generated by an LLM.
